implementation.name: N64 (MiSTer)
implementation.notes: Source availability (T5.4): open -- the repository carries 87 HDL source files (3 systemverilog, 6 verilog, 78 vhdl) alongside 10 prebuilt .rbf binaries. There is no open_source column in the delivered schema (data-model.md §1.9 deleted the proposed core table together with its flags); the presence of hdl_language_id and of implementation_path rows is how that fact is stated here. Machine mapping: hand-mapped, not MRA-setname-derived -- a console core ships no MRA files. The core reimplements the Nintendo 64, giving machine_id n64. Every id was checked against extract/machine.json. This console core doubles as an arcade core: Machine mapping: 11 arcade MRA files in Distribution_MiSTer/_Arcade naming <rbf>Aleck64</rbf> carry a <setname>; 11 resolved exactly to a MAME 0.288 machine and 0 through MAME's own cloneof relation to the parent set that survives extract/machine.json's parents-only filter, giving 11 distinct machine_id rows. Those setnames are MAME shortnames, so this part of the mapping is setname-derived. license_id omitted: the two license statements in the repository disagree. https://github.com/MiSTer-devel/N64_MiSTer/blob/main/LICENSE is the verbatim GNU GPL version 3 text, but the grant in https://github.com/MiSTer-devel/N64_MiSTer/blob/main/N64.sv offers the work under GPL version 2 or later. Either reading is arguable and neither is a fact the repository states, so no SPDX id is asserted. hdl_language_id: no single HDL family reaches 90% of the 87 source files (3 systemverilog, 6 verilog, 78 vhdl), excluding the shared framework directory. accuracy_id omitted: the repository makes no timing-fidelity claim this build could verify.
